name: Lazarus Street RipDoc Full Surgical Rig
description:
Ash-white poly-sealed surgical coat, hem cut asymmetrically to clear digitigrade legs or tail mods, over a moisture-wicking antimicrobial underlayer in pale green. Reinforced cuffs seal tight against chrome wrists; the back panel unzips into a sterile drape. Cargo trousers with instrument loops and an integrated knee pad — for crouching over a patient on a Shelf floor. Scuffed mag-closure boots with fluid-barrier soles.

A battered AR visor mounted on a worn headband serves as surgical display. Nitrile-analog gloves are permanently clipped to the left breast pocket. Nothing matches. Everything works.
functionality: Fluid-barrier coat and boots, sterile drape back panel, chrome-wrist sealed cuffs, AR surgical visor mount, instrument cargo loops, tail/digitigrade hem clearance, and antimicrobial underlayer for infection control in non-sterile environments.
what_it_says: You fix people that the licensed clinics turned away, and you haven't lost one yet — at least not to your mistakes.
story_hooks: The coat's serial number traces back to a Pellucid BioSeal licensed surgical set — reported stolen from a Tier 4 gene clinic three years ago.
A ripperdoc in this kit is the only person in the Shelf who knows how to remove a specific brand of corporate tracker implant.
The AR visor still has the previous owner's patient files cached — including someone very powerful who needed very quiet surgery.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian surgical ensemble designed for street medicine practitioners in ungoverned zones. The silhouette is deliberately asymmetrical and functional—white coat hanging loose over green underlayer, cargo trousers fitted for mobility, boots scuffed from concrete clinic floors. The overall impression is 'practiced chaos': pieces that were never meant to coordinate but have been worn into cohesion through countless emergency procedures.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately loose and unisex through the torso for movement and reach; cargo trousers taper at the ankle with reinforced knees for floor work; cuffs compress around augmented wrists; boots are wide-set for stability during long surgical hours.
physical_description.primary_material: Poly-sealed ash-white surgical coat (fluid-resistant synthetic blend), pale green antimicrobial underlayer (moisture-wicking bio-treated fabric), reinforced canvas cargo trousers, ballistic-weave knee panels, sealed rubber-compound boots with treaded soles.
physical_description.texture: Smooth poly-sealed exterior with subtle grip texture at contact points; underlayer is soft and breathable with faint ribbing; cargo fabric is worn and slightly distressed from use; boots show scuff marks and fluid residue staining.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant ash-white coat with pale sage-green underlayer visible at collar and cuffs; charcoal-gray cargo trousers; dark brown or black scuffed boots. Accent colors from worn AR visor (faded crimson display band) and chrome wrist seals (gunmetal gray).
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap closures on coat front (some slightly misaligned from repeated field repairs); heavy-duty zipper running full length of back panel; friction-fit wrist seals; magnetic closures on cargo pockets; mag-snap boots for quick removal during contamination protocols.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical hemline cut high on one side to accommodate digitigrade or tail modifications
Full-length back panel that unzips into a sterile drape for rapid surgical field setup
Instrument loops and suture anchor points sewn throughout trousers
Reinforced knee pad with integrated padding—worn flat from kneeling
Permanently clipped nitrile-analog glove set on left breast pocket
Battered AR visor mounted on adjustable headband, display screen showing faint scan artifacts
Visible repair stitching and patch work on cuffs and pocket edges
Fluid barrier soles on boots with non-slip tread pattern
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Sub-grade—this is street medicine equipment, affordable and salvageable, owned by practitioners outside corpo medical networks.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Shelf doctors, black-market surgeons, and emergency medics in the ungoverned zones of the GLMZ. The wearer is someone who performs urgent surgery in unsafe conditions—infection control is a luxury they've engineered into fabric, not infrastructure. Signifies practical expertise, risk tolerance, and marginalization from official healthcare.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily broken-in and weathered. Stains (some unidentifiable) on the coat hem and boot soles; visible mending on pockets and seams; the AR visor flickers intermittently; wrist seals show wear grooves from hundreds of seal/unseals; gloves at the breast pocket are yellowed and frayed at the edges.
